Sport Squad Jump Shot Pro - Easy Fold Indoor Electronic Basketball Arcade Game with Multi-Game Modes for Two Players - Basketball Game for Kids and Adults - Includes Four 7" Basketballs and Air Pump This is a wonderful game! Fun for the whole family, its got us away from our phones, and throwing balls through hoops. Which is not as easy as it first sounds.
After opening the box, it took about three hours to put it all together - when done, its wonderful. The computer in my one didn't work, which is great - it gives s reviewers a chance to find out what the technical support is like. And the technical support was wonderful. Quickly and easily the matter was resolved, a new scoreboard was sent to me, and all the details so I can return the old one.

This thing is big! Even folded up it has quite a big footprint. When you unfold it, lock the wheels, switch it on and grab the remote, the games begin.
You can play one or two player. The crowd roars, the count down rings, the buzzer goes, and the race is on! The remote control allows you to pause the game, add time, switch from one player to two players and switch the sound off (why would you want to?)

This really is a lot of fun. I have thought about getting one of these before and never did. I really wish I had. Fun for all the family and guests too!

Its very well designed and constructed, the free standing game doesn't slide at all on our garage (concrete) floor or on a carpeted floor. Its not hard to build, I did it on my own. Would be faster with two of you. The parts are solid, very well put together, the instructions are fantastic - I have put together a lot of "build it yourself" projects and these are the best, clearest instructions I have ever worked with.

Well worth the price, you wont want to stop playing!

text_fidelity_a:
Lezyne Road Drive HP High Pressure Road Bike Hand Pump, 160psi, Presta Valve Only, Gravel, Track Bicycle Over the decades of commuting, racing and just fun riding I've owned too many frame/mini pumps. Frame fit Silca Impero was still the standard against a handful of Zefals, Crank Brothers used. New top pump is the Lezyne Road Drive large size.

Strokes to reach and level of effort at 100psi:
Road Drive= 150 strokes at an easy-moderate effort
Pressure Drive (med) = 140 strokes at a moderate-hard effort
Silca Impero 520mm size = 120 strokes (90psi) at hard effort

The Road Drive is ~3mm narrower than the Pressure Drive. Maybe why it takes less effort at any psi above 70. Longer stroke more or less made up for the difference in air volume delivered.

The Lezyne pumps required a threaded valve stem. The pump is connected to the valve stem by a flexible length of hose that screws onto the pump when in use. Stored within the pump. Reduces the chance of snapping off a valve stem.

Found out the pump is relatively sturdy. The old Kirkland seat wedge pack has a pump sleeve. The large size Road Drive sticks out ~6cm. It ended up popping out hitting the pavement & bouncing a few times. Outside of couple cosmetic scuffs the pump works fine. A velcro strap now makes sure the pump stays put. At the Lezyne site rebuild kits are available. Nice not to have to chuck another pump into the landfill when time & wear ends a pumps usefulness.
text_fidelity_b: Lezyne Road Drive HP High Pressure Road Bike Hand Pump, 160psi, Presta Valve Only, Gravel, Track Bicycle

text_fidelity_a:
YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments My wife and I prefer weights as a workout, but both of us find the handles our community provides for the lat pull to be uncomfortable. The community provides the bar and nylon strap options, but 1. even with leather gloves they are uncomfortable, and 2. as a shorter guy my arm span is not such that I can get and maintain a comfortable reach (I can't hold the rubber grips on the bar), so for safety and comfort, I'm outta luck. But when I saw this YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for the gym I thought it might help me with comfort and safety, and be something she and I could both use to help improve.

The YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment is as easy as any attachment for the lat pull to get on and off, fitting the community's machine easily. There is a concern we have, but only time will tell if it plays out: the connection has a plastic exterior over what appears to be a metal disk, but we cannot tell how far that metal extends. It SEEMS as though it is only a disk and that the majority of the top piece is plastic. So we are not sure for how long or how much weight this connector will last. It is not that we have "proof" of it being subpar, just concerning by appearance.

The material of the rope itself also seems, not as overall strong, but as we are not at all experts in these materials or what is common in most of the heavy work gyms, we have nothing to compare it to. So we are going with it being an appropriate set up and provided materials. For our level of weights, even as I get stronger, we don't see it being at all an issue.

Lastly is the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment's handgrip, where you get that ergonomic element. I attempt to show in the various images how it is structured, curveted for the hand to rest within, allowing for a strong and comfortable grip. Again, I'm a shorter guy, so I also have a smaller hand. My wife's fingers are slightly longer than mine. We each find that the grip is both good and bad. We can each grip it and feel we have a secure hold. We feel safe. We feel a great pull. However, we each have a spot on the grip where it cuts into our finger/hand and begins to rub. In two images I show 1. the grip itself as I hold it up, then 2. my thumb over the top - it is at this point for me where it rubs and begins to feel like it's cutting into the thumb. Again, it is my hand size. My wife's issue is in the palm. She can fully and comfortably grip the handle, but at the base of the palm there is a cutting pressure.

So, do we like the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment? Yes, very much.
In spite of the issue and admittedly, with only using it twice for our full reps, we do like it. I will add, we have not worn our gloves during these workouts. We normally do, but circumstances had us in there without them, so using our bare hands, we did come up with discomfort whereby we got through the workouts, but didn't go full out as the discomfort grew. BUT, we both feel like once we have on the leather gloves the issue will at the least decrease greatly enough so as to allow us a full on workout and be okay. I will update if that does not pan out. But for each of us, the better grip and the overall feel of the YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment as far as what we can do, how safe we feel, and even comfort to the greater part of our hands is enough. We went with the 4 star because of the issue, but WE THINK THAT if they were to add a more comfortable cushion (rubber, something) to the grip, this would be a great 5 star grip.
text_fidelity_b: YODOTE Ergonomic Tricep Rope Cable Attachment for Gym - Anti-Slip 36" Tricep Rope Pull Down Attachment Unique Rubber Grip for Full Palm Support, Pulley System LAT Pulldown Cable Machine Attachments

text_fidelity_a: SoundAsleep Camping Series Air Mattress with Eco-Friendly PVC - Included Rechargeable Air Pump - Queen Size I'm always wary of buying air mattresses since I've never had one last more than a couple seasons before constantly deflating during the night. I hope this one is different, and so far after 4 nights it's performed beautifully. The mattress is very comfortable and I noticed that part of the reason for this is that the air chambers go from side to side instead of lengthwise like some other models. This seems to different zones for support and I'll look for this in any future air mattress purchases. I experienced very little initial stretching which the instructions say is common for the first few nights. I slept on it for 3 nights and only added a tiny bit of air the last night just to see how firm it would get. A nice touch is that the sides are slightly higher than the middle, which is very subtle but I'm sure keeps you from rolling off during the night. It comes with a good quality storage bag which sould help protect it when stored. The rechargable pump works well for inflating and deflating and comes with an AC adapter, car charger, and a couple different nozzles. Actually, the charger is the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars - for two reasons. First, it has NiCd batteries which are pretty old school in terms of rechargeables and won't last very long, at which point it becomes a brick. Ominously, perhaps they are only meant to last as long as the mattress? Second, the charger and accessories don't come with any kind of stuff sack or even a pocket in the mattress bag. I nice little cheapo storage sack for the charger and accessories is really needed. Other than that, so far so good. Very comfortable mattress.
text_fidelity_b: SoundAsleep Camping Series Air Mattress with Eco-Friendly PVC - Included Rechargeable Air Pump - Queen Size

text_fidelity_a:
ANOOPSYCHE Bodyweight Fitness Resistance Trainer Kit with Body Workout Guide, Fitness Training Straps for Home or Professional Complete Body Workout Seems to be a good quality piece of workout equipment. Nice and versatile. The web strapping is a good thickness. Surprising how heavy it was in the box. I have a similar product from Golds Gym. This one from Anoopsyche is thicker and heavier.

Perhaps my favorite thing about this product is that the two handles are separate, which makes doing exercises (pushing, pulling, and foot in strap) much more comfortable than with one that is connected at the top.

A close second is the versatility in setting it up. It'll wrap around a bar or wedge in a closed door.

It also includes a strap that connects both sides to one mounting spot. Honestly, I'm not sure why. It's plenty long separated. Combined I think that it would be overly long unless your mounting to an extra high mounting spot. You could probably mount this thing ten foot off the ground with the additional strap without a problem. Personally, the handle sections alone are enough for me.

The buckles seem to be good quality buckles.

Deducting one star for quality control. The two handle straps are different lengths. Which is a mute point because the straps are adjustable. Just causes me to have to double check that I've adjusted both straps to equal lengths. You figure out pretty quick when both hands are in different positions because of different lengths. I ordered a second set at the same time for a friend. I opened that box to check the length of the straps. In that box both straps were the same length. I'll continue using the odd length ones and give the friend the even length ones for their convenience.
text_fidelity_b: ANOOPSYCHE Bodyweight Fitness Resistance Trainer Kit with Body Workout Guide, Fitness Training Straps for Home or Professional Complete Body Workout

text_fidelity_a: Power Pro Spectra Fiber Braided Fishing Line I LOVE this fishing line. not only is it a good color that blends in well with most fishing environments, but it's crazy strong! All Pro Weight Adjustable Ankle Weights, 10-lb pair (up to 5-lbs per ankle) These are comfortable -- very well padded -- and the weight is easy to adjust. However, the product has a few issues:

B) Due to (A) I often try to really lock them down, and that's very tricky given the velcro fastening system. It would be very nice to have, in addition to the velcro, some way to tighten things further via a strap closure or something. (Or fix (A) using some different material.)

C) Probably also related to (A) -- they don't breathe very well. After a longer/harder session they can be a bit wet.

None of these are really a big deal, thus I only removed a single star. I think this is a quality product. And I think all of these defects could probably be fixed the same way, by reconsidering the material on the inside of the strap. Anyway, despite these minor flaws I'm happy with the purchase, and am already looking at buying a pair of the company's 10-lb weights to add to the mix.

Frankford Arsenal Quick-N-EZ 110V Case Tumbler Kit with Sifter for Brass Cartridge Cleaning and Polishing for Reloading [[VIDEOID:4d97ce6c49de579dc9b8d7678abf3b9f]] Maybe it is a little early for this review since I got this yesterday but I am very impressed and this has been run about 16 hours out of the last 20. I set it on a smart plug timer so it could even do a late night batch without running all night. I used to do ultrasonic cleaning but I hated the drying process and the less pleasing lack of that brassy shine you get with tumbling.
A couple pieces of advice....I saw reviewers mentioning the center bolt dinging up brass, the fix is SUPER easy. A simple drinking straw to cover the threads. I even found a blue one that matches the tumbler.
Second piece of advice, don't be dumb like me. I had a handful of .223 that I decided to add to the .40 cal I was tumbling. .223 fits in the .40 cal so many of the .223 had unpolished bases. Just remember 9 mm fits in .40 and .40 fits in .45. so pay attention if you mix brass. Make sure it can't fit inside the other type.
text_fidelity_b: Frankford Arsenal Quick-N-EZ 110V Case Tumbler Kit with Sifter for Brass Cartridge Cleaning and Polishing for Reloading

Jetson Kids 2-Wheel Light-Up Kick Scooter | Includes LED Lights on Handlebar, Stem, Wheels & Deck | Adjustable Handlebar | Rear Brake | Lightweight Design | Easy-Folding Mechanism, Ages 5+ This is a scooter that will earn a lot of points for uniqueness. None of the kids in the neighborhood have seen anything like it. It appears to have very good construction overall from a stability standpoint, and I don't feel like it's going to fall apart any time soon. Construction is literally one screw and one nut, although it's awkward to install given that both screw head and nut are recessed into the structure.

That said, there are a few questionable design points that lower it's score for us. The lights are controlled by batteries rather than the motion of the wheels, the latter of which would not only save us from replacing the batteries as frequently as we are, but also would keep us from having to adjust them, which we need to do on a pretty consistent basis. It's a scooter, so it sees some pretty rough play, and that can often jar a battery loose since they don't sit particularly tightly.

In addition to this, despite my comment about overalll good construction, the switch that controls whether it is folded or open is made of some very cheap plastic, and appears likely to break quickly, espeically with how difficult it is to pull when tightened.

Overall, it's a gimmick that, if you really want to put up with, is pretty cool. For an everyday use item, you probably want something simpler that won't require constant monitoring.

But I can slice it with the best of them, so more practice will be necessary if I ever want to fully get rid of this weakness.

I enjoy the driver and the adjustable loft is an added bonus. I set it at what I think will work and leave it at that. Again, my inexperience doesn't allow for a consistent golf swing so I'll sometimes launch it into the stratosphere or run it a foot off the ground for seventy five yards--or something in between--regardless of the loft setting. Again, no technology will replace technique, but I like the feel and swing, and am very happy with the purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Cobra 2017 Golf Men's King F7 Driver Connect

text_fidelity_a:
PRETTYGAGA Plus Holds Cell Phone，Outdoor Tactical， Messenger Bag， Military Trekking As a woman who wants to enjoy the concealed carry option but doesn’t want to carry an extra purse for cell phone, cash, etc., I have to say this little case takes care of it all. It has so much functionality that I almost don’t know where to start.

Laying flat and without anything in it, this very durable and well-made nylon case measures about 7-1/2” wide x 9-1/2” tall. That also includes a gusset which, when extended, accommodates a pretty good sized gun. Almost all the seams are double-stitched, and an outer strong and durable bungee style closure keeps the pockets on the outer side of the purse secure. In addition to the larger inner pocket where you can stash your weapon (or if not a weapon will hold quite a bit of other things), there is also a front outer pocket that is perfect for a cell phone. My Galaxy J7 fits great. Another great feature is you have the option of carrying this case like a purse with the removable strap, or you can remove the strap and wear on your belt.

There is a wide band of Velcro in the front of the case which, when opened reveals 10 card slots (including 1 clear for I.D.), a zippered pocket which is perfect size for cash bills, and a pocket behind each set of card slots where you can store coupons, receipts, etc. **I do want to note that while the zipper pouch is great for bills, it may not be great for loose change because if you unzipper the bill slot with the case in upright/vertical position which it would be if you are wearing it, and loose change may fall out. There is also a zipper pocket right at the very top of the purse actually at the top of the front flap. Unzip that and you’ll find a great little pocket for an extra magazine (or 2-3 depending on the size). It could also be a good pocket to hold your keys. On the back side of this pouch there is another zipper compartment that can easily hold a larger size cell phone or extra ammo mags or even your gun depending on the size.

Overall, this is a great case that can be used by men or women, and I can’t find anything that I don’t like about it. It’s a keeper!
text_fidelity_b: PRETTYGAGA Plus Holds Cell Phone，Outdoor Tactical， Messenger Bag， Military Trekking

The problem with assembly, and the reason that some of the reviewers say that it's easier to assemble after you've done it several times, is that the side rails are approximately the same size as the canvas sleeves you have to put them in. I assume that the canvas will stretch with several assemblies. So when you assemble it, you have to push on it until the canvas stretches to fit the rails. That is no easy task. Once you have inserted the side rails, you have to rotate them. I did that by putting a screwdriver in the holes that need to match up with the slits in the canvas and working it back-and-forth until the rails were rotated. Again, no easy task. Once you do that, you put one end of the spring steel legs in one of the holes of the rails, and compress the spring steel so that you can get the other end in the other set of holes on the other side of the cot. While I was doing this, I was imagining a trip to the emergency room if the spring steel leg slipped out of my hand.

If you can deal with all of this, then it seems comfortable.

I guess it will serve my needs.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Lightweight Cot

Texan Classics Utility Hybrid Iron-Wood #2 Golf Club OK - my own fault as by now, I know you get what you pay for. On this basis, buying a $20 hybrid is more experiment than sensible purchase. But based on prior reviews, I thought, why not?

Here's why not: I received the club on Wednesday, put it in my bag and went to the course on Thursday. Looks like a Taylormade Rescue, but with really poor detail. Well, looks don't get the ball down the course, and it was $20, so who cares, right?

First shot, nicely impressed...second shot, the same. Third shot, I feel something...odd. Ball pops straight up in the air at almost a 90 degree angle to my lie. Look at the club, and there's the answer. Clubhead is an inch down the shaft from the ferrule, and with the slightest tug, it pops right off. So much for the experiment.

Maybe I'm crazy, but there's just no excuse for a clubhead falling off within three shots; six swings total with practice. None. Zero. I'm surprised it actually made it through shipping without coming off. Maybe they used cornstarch to glue this on instead of epoxy? Who knows. The only saving grace is that I hadn't yet thrown away the box, so it was easy to return this dismal thing.
text_fidelity_b: Texan Classics Utility Hybrid Iron-Wood #2 Golf Club

text_fidelity_a:
Thule 9001 Raceway 2 Bike Trunk Mounted Bike Rack, Black, One Size 3000 mile round trip with 2 road bikes at 85mph and we couldn't be happier. It took me about 3 minutes to figure out the install and another 3 minutes to load up the bikes. The rack holds extremely steady with virtually no movement from the bikes and requires little, if any, tightening once underway. Just as other user mentioned, we did have some damage to the lower bumper, a slight indention and a little peeling of the clear coat, but I don't hold that against this product. Really its just the ABS plastic bumper that was the issue and its hardly a problem. As for the trunk lid, there was absolutely no damage or markings at all. The color of the product is slightly misrepresented in the pictures - its more of a flat, colorless black composite than a shiny black color. Again, this is no issue for me, just not exactly what I expected. I will say, I'd guess this product could easily be painted to match your vehicle if you really wanted a cool, custom look. One other unexpected issue was the loss of MPG. We were driving a Honda Civic that regularly gets 30+mpg and that fell to 25-27mpg. Once more, no issue with the product, just something to be aware of for those on a longer drive.

On the whole, this rack is super easy to use, looks a LOT nicer than other racks, heavy enough to feel solid, light enough to store with ease. Over he course of our 3000 mile journey, I took this on and off 6 times and I never begrudged doing it. I would highly recommend this bike rack to anyone that asked.

Tips: Make sure the points of contact are clean before putting the rack on. This will ensure no dirt gets trapped and acts like sand paper once moving. Use small bungies or velcro straps to secure your front wheel from spinning and one more to secure the pedals of the two bikes to each other so the cranks don't turn. The security cable is a very nice touch that I would have no problem trusting for cross town and short stops, but I still added a standard, coated bike cable to secure it to the rack to feel more comfortable stopping overnight as the provided cable could very easily be cut with a small bolt cutter. Load your heavier bike on first to reduce the leverage placed on the rack. Take a short test run before going a long distance.
text_fidelity_b: Thule 9001 Raceway 2 Bike Trunk Mounted Bike Rack, Black, One Size

text_fidelity_a:
Camp Chef Everest 2 Burner Stove Update 8/21/17 - Just returned from a 5 day camping trip where I used this stove every meal and I have to drop my rating from 3 stars down to 1. Here are the reasons why I don't like this stove:
1. Extremely poor flame control. It's impossible to get and keep a low flame. If you manage to get it low enough, the slightest breeze will blow it out. Had numerous boil-overs and burnt food from the high heat.
2. No handle, or easy places to grab. This issue went from a nuisance to a real PITA the more I had to move it around.
3. No protection for the knobs/piezo lighter. They will eventually get damaged without protection.
4. Nowhere to easily hold the stove while depressing the piezo lighter with one hand. Again, a seeminly minor nuisance that turned into a real PITA - especially when the stove it hot from the left burner and trying to light the right burner.
5. No type of anti-skid on the bottom of the stove. If you're using any kind of slick surface, like a camp kitchen, it will slide all over the place especially when trying to light the burners.

I’ll jump to the bottom line first – if you’re looking for a high quality, durable camp stove that will last for decades – they don’t seem to exist anymore. Like so many of today’s products, they are manufactured to last a season or two and then replaced with the next great thing. To be fair, I’m comparing it to what it’s replacing: my 50+ year old Coleman dual fuel. But, the more I look at these new stoves, the more I think I’ll just stick with my old one. It still works great, I just wanted a new and shiny two-burner and the convenience of propane.

Here’s the highlights:

Pros
Stylish
Lightweight (can also be a con)
Size
Cleanup

Cons
Fit and finish
Shoddy workmanship
Cheap rivets
Poor temperature control on low
Plastic lid latches
Regulator
Poor two-burner flame on a small bottle
No handle

I did a lot of research and really wanted to love this stove (still do). My current camp kitchen consists of a Coleman 413E gas stove and a Coleman 5418 single burner propane stove. Little did I know that I’ve been cooking on vintage stoves for many years! I recently added a Camp Chef EX60 two burner Explorer with a large steel griddle. Yes, this was a MAJOR upgrade. It’s a beast and requires a big propane bottle. Don’t know what I was thinking, but I love it.

After the disappointment of this Camp Chef Everest, I did a lot more research and went out and actually touchy/feely’d all the other comparable stoves I could find at REI, Walmart, Target, etc. I’ll just say that I think all of these stoves, regardless of brand name, come from the same completely unsupervised and un-credentialed factory in China. There may be minor differences, but there are too many similarities to be coincidence.

So here’s the details on the Pros: It looks pretty. Sitting in your campsite it will be the envy of the campground. And when you splatter grease all over it when cooking, at least it wipes down fairly easily. It can fit a 12” and 10.5” skillet at the same time centered over the burners with the windscreens up. That’s nice. And it’s light - because it’s made out of thin stamped metal and lightweight pop-rivets.

Now for the Cons. I figured almost nothing else mattered if it performed. But it doesn’t, and so everything else does matter. Ask yourself why you think you need a “high output/high BTU” stove. Presumably to boil water faster. It’s certainly not for cooking because you’ll never use high output for regular cooking. And high output does not equate to better performance. I’ll bet there are 11,000 BTU burners that will boil water just as fast as these. Frankly, these burners just don’t perform very well at low, medium, or high settings. At the very lowest setting there is a huge yellow flame that just won’t go away. Same on high. Only somewhere in the middle do you find a sweet spot for the flame, but it’s too hot for normal cooking. With two burners going, the small propane bottle just can’t keep up and both flames become unmanageable. I didn’t try using the bigger bottle lacking a hose. Which brings me to the regulator. It’s garbage, I don’t trust it, and I’m sure it will fail in short order. Both of the points where the tube joins the connectors shows very poor quality control. Not to mention it’s crooked when hooked up to the stove – meaning the connector part of the stove is not centered in the hole.

All of the bad reviews you read about poor fit and finish are true. There are sharp edges where the drip pan meets the body. The wind screens don’t line up without actually bending the pieces to achieve a “custom fit”, but that’s easy because the metal is flimsy and they used cheap pop-rivets which insures everything is loosely attached. The hinges that attach the top to the bottom are a joke – stamped aluminum and poorly attached with pop-rivets. There is no way the plastic lid latches are going to last – I’m surprised they survived shipping. I can’t stress enough how un-durable this stove is. But, it’s exactly the same as all the others.

To test out the cooking ability, I’ve cooked 3 things: pan roasted potatoes, pan roasted cross-cut ribs – both in cast iron skillets, and scrambled eggs in a non-stick pan. All 3 of these require good temperature control at low to medium-low setting. Note: I can do all of these perfectly on my Coleman 513E. On the lowest setting, my potatoes were over-crisped before cooking completely through. The cross-cut ribs probably would have been ok, but I missed the sweet spot for a second and they over-cooked. The scrambled eggs actually turned out ok, but I was very careful and moved the pan on and off the flame as needed while cooking. All in all, I think you can turn out good food on this stove, but for me it’s going to take way too much attention and fussing. I think I want something with lower BTU burners that perform and adjust better.
text_fidelity_b: Camp Chef Everest 2 Burner Stove

Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Hitch Mount Rack , Silver/Black (522RR) Believe the reviews that say this is terrific! I had some concerns about the small receiver shaft wobbling in my 2-inch hitch, but Allen Sports has really figured it out with their "wobble bolt." My rig is tight and vibration free.

From the pictures it looked like the plates on the hitch were plastic shims, but they are well-designed (removable) plates screwed to the main shaft. And their design -- again -- contributes to the rigidity of the frame when mounted.

I mounted this rack in less than 10 minutes, threw on the bikes and drove 700+ miles without any issues whatsoever. Bikes arrived without a scratch and as secure as they were when I left the driveway.

There are only three factors of this hitch that I'll point out:
1) It is an inch or two higher than it needs to be, so the bikes are in the rear window of my SUV. (This could be an adjustable setting of the rack if Allen Sports (or I, I suppose) would drill a couple of different holes in the upper piece of the rack.)
2) It does trigger the proximity sensors in my rear bumper. So I had to dig through the owner's manual to figure out how to disable that.

As others have mentioned, the frame of the bike will bang on the vertical section of the rack if not attended to. I wrapped a thin sheet of foam rubber around the upright and secured it with some black duct tape I had handy. You can't even see the pad, and it cushions the frame of the first bike when tied down with a bungee cord.

My favorite feature of this rack is the tilting mechanism. It makes it trivially easy to move the bikes out of the way for access through the tailgate.

Overall, one of my best Amazon purchases this year. I've compared Yakima and Thule racks at 3-5+ times the price and can't find anything in them that is superior to this one.
text_fidelity_b: Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Hitch Mount Rack , Silver/Black (522RR)

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) My first Charge 2 was wonderful until it stopped reading my HR correctly after 5 months. My Charge 2 would tell me that my HR was 130+ when I was sitting or not even wearing it. On top of that, the wristband broke around the same time. I contacted support and they tried to fix the problem by having me restart my Fitbit however it did not work. Customer support was nice enough to offer me a replacement after going back and forth a few times.

Unfortunately the replacement Fitbit sent me was defective. I put the Fitbit on and tighten the wristband and position the Fitbit to the correct spot on my wrist but the Fitbit would not pickup my HR. After a few hours it started to read my HR however the reading was completely off. I took the Fitbit off and it continued to give me an outrageously high HR. It said my HR was 150 when I was just sitting or not wearing it. That's riduculous! I tried resetting the Fitbit many times but it did not solve the problem. I ended up wearing the Fitbit for a few months to see if it was just a one time fluke (I was also too lazy and feeling too frustrated to contact customer support AGAIN). Unfortunately the Charge 2 continued to read my heart rate incorrectly. To add onto the problem, this new Fitbit would think I'm walking when I'm just driving. I understand that most Fitbit will do this sometimes but mines was doing it all the time! No way I walked closed to 10000 steps each day. I've been lazy as F and I've been doing a lot of sitting these past few months LOL.

I finally found some free time today and hollered at customer service. They asked me to reset my Fitbit, so I did, but as I was doing so, my Fitbit battery suddenly drained and my Fitbit died. WHAT? After waiting for my Fitbit to come back to life the rep asked me to fire up the app and sync my Fitbit to the app. We tried 5 times and even reset the app but it didn't work. UGH this is now the FOUTH issue I'm having with this Charge 2. What a nightmare.

The rep quickly offered me a 50% discount for a new device or get my Fitbit Charge 2 replaced. NO WAY was I willing to get a THIRD Charge 2 and risk having to go through the headache of contacting customer service again if my THIRD Fitbit turns out to be defective too. I pestered the rep to see if she could give me a better discount, refund me, or give me credit to upgrade to a better model. Sadly, the rep and the supervisor did not have the power to offer me a better deal.

*When I asked for a refund or credit for a better model, the rep responded with this:

"I really understand your frustration Kimberly, however please be assured that our product team is constantly working to ensure that our products go through rigorous testing so that they can last and endure as expected."

LIES! Obviously Fitbit doesn't tell well enough if I've received two defective Charge 2.

*I asked if my warranty will be extended if I obtain a THIRD Charge 2:

Rep - If the device is out of warranty we will be unable to replace it and we may offer a discount to purchase a new device.
Rep - I understand your concern Kimberly, but if you decide to use the 50% discount to make a upgrade the new device will have a new warranty.
Rep - When you receive a replacement device, the replacement device has 30 days of warranty or the remaining of the original warranty.
Rep - So if the device fails which is not something that we expect to happen you have 30 days from the moment that the device is received in order to contact us again and get a replacement if necessary.

Sigh, this offer is not good enough. I wonder if I can sue for giving me a headache if my THIRD Fitbit also turns out to be defective...

*I then inquired about what happens if I have to claim a FOURTH Fitbit?

Me: would I qualify for a different model at that point
Me: or just another 50 % off discount
Rep: That would be a very unusual situation Kimberly and to answer your question, the amount of replacement devices that you receive does not makes you applicable for a free upgrade since that is a program that we don't have at the moment.
Me: Is it unusual that I received two fit bits that do not work
Me: Or is this fairly common
Rep: The reason is that the two devices that you have received failed in different areas Kimberly. Even this is not an expected situation.

Uh huh....

*Lastly, I asked if I will be sent a refurbished Charge 2 if I choose the replacement option:

Rep: Depending on available inventory, we sometimes issue factory-certified refurbished products as warranty replacements. These are typically products that were returned to Fitbit unused for reasons like wrong size and wrong color.
Me: Well that's not good
Rep: In most cases however, warranty replacements are brand new products that we package without accessories for easier shipping.
Me: how Do I guarantee that I get a NEW one
Rep: Since that depends on the warehouse Kimberly we have no control about if a new or factory-certified refurbished device will be sent.

I really wished Fitbit had a better buyer protection plan for unfortunate people like me. If you're reading this Fitbit, I would really like my money back or an upgrade to the Blaze or Ionic.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version)

Is it quite as nice in the fit/finish as the expensive ones? nope. But so far, it's got some great design features and doesn't feel rickety at all.

Goes together easily, every tube is elasticized to the hole. If the elastic ever breaks, you can still assemble it easily, so don't sweat that.

You assemble it by first putting the bottom of the chair on the posts (after you get all the posts stuck together) and then in the pockets where the upper poles mount are... two finger rings! absolutely genius! they make stretching the fabric tightly enough to fit the poles a breeze. Great little idea.

It's small enough to fit into a backpack but holds my 6'3, 180lb butt so comfortably. It's a good seating position, you can recline in it or sit hunched forward for eating, so the ergos are spot on. Very balanced to sit in, doesn't feel like you'll fall at all. Sure, it's a couple pounds, but when you get to camp and your friends are all sitting on a cold, wet log trying to find the good spot around the fire, you'll be lounging in comfort.

I was skeptical about the brightness of the flashlight feature. It appears to be a fairly large COB with a projection (magnifying) lens over it. I used it in my backyard tonight and it’s just about as bright as a standard LED flashlight.
The strobes are a cool feature. I hope to never use them in an emergency but have some fun playing with them with my kids. The magnetic base is cool too. Good for use under a car hood or under the vehicle itself. Strong enough magnets to keep it in its place.

The battery life Is to be determined. I haven’t had this one long enough to go through the internal battery and I haven’t put AA’s in it yet. I’m not sure I will. I love the fact this is rechargeable and even though we all have the cables, this came with 2 of them. Nice touch.
It would be nice to see the handles coated (rubberized or similar). I’ve seen some nice lanterns that have that, but at double or more the cost of these.

Lanzom® Outdoor Camouflage Bucket Hats Mesh Sun Hat Boonie Fishing Hats The orange hat I ordered was SO UGLY that I actually had to order a different color (the navy) for myself at full price so I could write a fair review. I was fortunate to be able to purchase the orange one at a discount and I was hoping to receive the bright, punchy tangerine color shown in the example image. Instead I received a burnt orange hat with a bright orange mesh band and all of it is HIDEOUS. I was so upset that I had "wasted" my discount! Luckily my 9 year old is willing to wear the hat which is good because I can't return it. I can promise you this orange hat will never be stolen. EVER.

The pictures I included were taken in natural daylight and they don't accurately capture just how ugly and mis-matched the orange hat is. The body of the hat is a burnt blood orange color. It is remarkably ugly, even for University of Texas fans. The mesh band is safety orange - very similar to the neon orange color deer hunters sometimes wear. In person, the colors clash so badly that it really is only appropriate for a 9 year old boy to wear because it is assumed he doesn't know any better. And even then it is only suitable to wear fishing. Alone, so no one sees the hat. On a windy lake where you have the best chance of losing it.

The Navy hat is a million times better. It, too, does not match its example image but in a good way. The hat is a deep, dark midnight navy shade with a dark navy band that matches the hat body. It looks very nice. If I could do it over again I would select the black or navy for myself. Anything but this orange hat!

The hat itself is very comfortable and lightweight. I love the feel of it, how breathable it is and that the strap is very loose and lightweight. (I can't stand the feeling of things around my chin and neck or the sensation that cords are choking me.) This hat is pleasantly comfortable, bounces back from being crushed (or thrown across the room and trampled underfoot until the navy hat arrived because it was so danged ugly) and it seems like it will shed water well if splashed.

I was fortunate to be able to purchase this hat at a discount, I just picked the wrong color. I liked the hat well enough to buy it at full price in another color that I am actually willing to wear. I REALLY wished I had bought any color but the orange! I hope that by sharing my experience and photos that you are able to make the best buying decision! (Hint: ORANGE is the wrong answer!)
text_fidelity_b: Lanzom® Outdoor Camouflage Bucket Hats Mesh Sun Hat Boonie Fishing Hats

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman White Water Adult Sleeping Bag, Big & Tall Our family does a lot of camping due to the boys and myself being in a scouting organization and enjoying the outdoors. I have been camping since I was a kid and have slept in numerous sleeping bags and have owned numerous coleman sleeping bags. I bought this Coleman White Water Large Cool-Weather Scoop Sleeping Bag from Amazon when it was a lightning deal back in November 2015. I have used the bag solely on our camp-outs since then. I have slept in it over a dozen nights under the stars in different temperature and weather conditions. Majority of the nights have been clear and low humidity with temperatures between 35-65 degrees.

This bag could sleep one and a half people (me and one of my kids) or one large person hence the name “large” in the title. In the description on Amazon says the bag is designed for 30-50 degree weather. We spent one weekend under the stars in the lower to mid 30s and it was cold and needed another blanket, however other nights between 40-60 degrees it is very comfortable.

So I would rate this sleeping bag 40 degrees and above. We do live in Georgia and humidity is high even in the winter time so in another climate 30 degrees may be comfortable in this bag. I liked that it is very comfortable sleeping on the ground with one of the most comfortable interiors of any sleeping bag i have slept in. The sleeping bag is made of 100% Polyester with 100% cotton fill. Overall a great deal if you can find it on sale.

Positives:
+Oversized for comfort
+Zipper does not get stuck in the material
+Comfortable (40-60 degrees)
+Five year warranty on stitching and workmanship

Negatives:
-Is not comfortable low to mid 30s
-Does not come with storage bag
text_fidelity_b: Coleman White Water Adult Sleeping Bag, Big & Tall

text_fidelity_a:
Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle I had a couple older magnesium stick fire starter for years and was really excited to try this out. Most people I've listened to swear by them.
Here are the PROs:
- This performs medium to well for giving you a spark. Having never used one (and probably using poor technique), I was still able to generate a decent spark at least 1 out of every 2-3 strikes.
- Doubles as a whistle. This thing actually works extremely well. If you ever need it, it's simple and high-pitched, a great space-saver.
- Feels good to use. I'd rate it at around 6 out of 10. It's a little short and I found the striker attached to the steel via the cord a little restricting, but the thumb grooves make up for it. It's funny how a small depression in plastic can make that much of a difference in comfort.

Here are the CONs:
- This requires that you have good tender or some type of fuel/accelerant. I miss having my pile of magnesium scrapings to be honest. While it's another piece of equipment, I'm probably going to keep my magnesium stick with me. It seems like the majority of times I've gone packing or camping, it's been damp out, and finding a decent amount of usable tender isn't always a sure bet.
- A little small. This is my complaint with just about any striker. They're just about a 1/4"-1/5" too small to be really comfortable. This is being picky, but still worth mentioning.

Overall, I'm enjoying using this thing and I'll probably make it a mainstay of my gear.
text_fidelity_b: Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle

text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Frontiersman 9.2 oz. Bear Spray, Maximum Strength 2.0% Major Capsaicinoids, Powerful 35 ft. Range Bear Deterrent, Outdoor Camping & Hiking Protection, Quick Draw Holster & Multipack Options Just like verifying that you are comfortable using a pistol or rifle, you also have to know that any weapon that you have reason to depend on is functional and loaded. It's only common sense to test out any weapon prior to depending on it to defend yourself and/or your family. A firearm that goes "click" when you pull the trigger is of no use to you -- and neither is this Sabre Bear Spray if the can/fixture is faulty or filled with ineffective spray.

When I was in the pepper spray distribution business many years ago, I always had to test out sample batches of the product to make sure that the sprayer worked and the spray itself was as powerful as promised. I got tired of being sprayed in the face (like all police officers who carry a personal defense spray are required to do) so I devised an alternative test that was not as intrusive or disabling.

Taking the canister outside of our building, I'd find a quiet space with no wind and spray a small amount on the back of my hand. That accomplishes two things; it shows that the can is pressurized and discharges properly and it also demonstrates how irritating the spray is to the back of your hand. As you will find out for yourself, a good can will provide an instant burning sensation. However you must be extremely careful to not get it in your eyes or transfer it to other parts of your exposed skin. That can end up being almost as bad as taking a full blast in the face.

My youngest daughter and my wife each carries one of these units. SABRE has always been highly regarded in the industry but in the past I did test one of their products and find it to be totally ineffective. They took care of the problem, replaced the faulty unit with a good one, and now I feel that my wife and daughter have the advantage in a confrontation should they practice "situational awareness" and keep their wits about them. I told them to keep spraying until the criminal, dog, or whatever threat targeting them is down for the count and does not remain a danger to them. They each have a concealed carry permit so I am confident that if they have to they can move on to the next step.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Frontiersman 9.2 oz. Bear Spray, Maximum Strength 2.0% Major Capsaicinoids, Powerful 35 ft. Range Bear Deterrent, Outdoor Camping & Hiking Protection, Quick Draw Holster & Multipack Options
